title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: The controls, commands and licensing statements are supported, including by the recently updated Copilot Studio documentation. Five navigation paths stop before the final control and need minor completion; no blocking discrepancies were found.

claims.claim: MCP connects Copilot Studio agents to existing knowledge servers and data sources.
claims.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) helps you connect to existing knowledge servers and data sources directly within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: An MCP server publishes tools and resources.
claims.quote: Each tool or resource that a connected MCP server publishes is automatically available for use in Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: A Copilot Studio agent can act as an MCP client and call the server's tools.
claims.quote: A single MCP server can integrate and manage multiple tools and resources. Copilot Studio agents can access each tool.

claims.claim: Resources are file-like data an agent can read.
claims.quote: Resources: File-like data that an agent can read for more context, such as API responses or file contents

claims.claim: Tools are functions a language model can call to perform an action.
claims.quote: Tools: Functions that a language model can call to perform an action

claims.claim: MCP prompts are predefined templates.
claims.quote: Prompts: Predefined prompt templates to accomplish specific tasks

claims.claim: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.

claims.claim: The MCP server supplies tool names, descriptions, inputs and outputs.
claims.quote: The server provides the name, description, inputs, and outputs.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio dynamically reflects tools added, updated or removed on the server.
claims.quote: When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: The standard-harness MCP guidance requires generative orchestration to be on.
claims.quote: You must turn on generative orchestration to use MCP.

claims.claim: The supported Copilot Studio MCP transport is Streamable.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio supports the Streamable transport type.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.

claims.claim: The MCP onboarding wizard offers None, API key and OAuth 2.0 authentication.
claims.quote:
You have three options:

- None
- API key: Configure API key authentication
- OAuth 2.0: Configure OAuth 2.0 authentication

claims.where: What it is: governance surfaces table
claims.claim: Power Platform connector data policies govern MCP access in Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Access to MCP servers in Copilot Studio relies on Power Platform connectors for connectivity. This condition means that if a data policy regulates Power Platform connectors, it also regulates access to the MCP server and its tools for your agent.

claims.where: What it is: governance surfaces table
claims.claim: Advanced connector policies can govern Power Platform MCP servers.
claims.quote: Advanced connector policies support visibility and management of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

claims.claim: Work IQ offers a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Federated connectors with the appropriate tools can create, update or delete connected-system data on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for querying records.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for creating rows.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for updating rows.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.claim: The general connectors overview still calls federated connectors read-only while announcing write actions from early October 2026.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: Plugin package-level actions are not separate controls for each included component.
claims.quote: These package-level actions aren't separate controls for each included component.

claims.where: What it is: governance surfaces table; Why it matters
claims.claim: Federated connector availability is governed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you manage federated connector availability in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: No licence or meter for the MCP protocol itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: MCP protocol itself license pricing fee protocol; read Copilot Studio MCP guidance, Dataverse MCP FAQ, Agent 365 service description, Work IQ overview and billing-credit-overview. Results describe client/server costs, not a protocol licence or meter.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 service description requires Microsoft 365 E7 / G7 or Agent 365 for tenant-wide tool access control, rather than including it in the listed Microsoft 365 plans.
claims.quote: Control which tools (including Microsoft MCP servers) agents can access tenant-wide | Microsoft 365 Admin Center | No | Yes | Yes

claims.claim: Agents on the Microsoft Copilot harness incur Copilot Credits for tools, including MCPs.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP tools are charged from 15 December 2025 when accessed by AI agents created outside Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Starting December 15, 2025, Dataverse MCP tools are charged when accessed by AI agents created outside of Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot USL holders are not charged for accessing Dynamics 365 data through Dataverse MCP.
claims.quote: If you have qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium licenses or a Microsoft 365 Copilot User Subscription License (USL), you aren't charged for accessing Dynamics 365 data.

claims.claim: A user needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to see a federated connector.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies support server-level blocking but not granular control of individual MCP tools.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: ACP immediately enforces a strict allowlist when saved for an environment or published for an environment group.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group): every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.claim: ACP does not yet support custom or HTTP connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.claim: Registry tool-level granular control is rolling out.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: Registry tool-level granular control supports only specific MCP server types.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: When a registry server does not support tool discovery, individual tools cannot be managed there and whole-server blocking is the documented alternative.
claims.quote: If an MCP server doesn't support tool discovery, the Tools tab shows a message that the server doesn't support tool discovery, and individual tools aren't available to manage.

claims.claim: Blocking an MCP server is a separate component-level action.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server is a separate component-level action;

claims.claim: Effects of MCP server blocking on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the management route.
claims.quote: effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the applicable management route.

claims.claim: Blocking a plugin leaves its associated MCP servers available to other plugins.
claims.quote: Associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio makes users responsible for the tools and resources accessed from non-Microsoft MCP servers.
claims.quote: When you connect to a non-Microsoft product, including an external MCP server, you're responsible for the tools and resources you access from within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements.

claims.claim: Disabling Dataverse MCP stops every tool and agent that relies on it.
claims.quote: Disabling the Dataverse MCP Server stops all tools and agents that rely on it.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp entrypoint.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the `/api/mcp` agent entrypoint.

claims.claim: MCP-named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and are not restricted by the MCP allow list.
claims.quote: MCP‑named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.
